questions.title: The questions a pitch won't answer
questions.intro: A polished pitch shows what an agency can make. These nine questions show how it thinks, who does the work and what you are really paying for. Tap each card to see how we answer.

items.question: Do I really need everything you’re selling?
items.teaser: Big packages look thorough, but they often spread your budget thin.
items.answer: Probably not, and we’ll tell you which parts you can skip. We start from where your brand is today and recommend only the phases that will move it at this stage. Some brands need an audit and a clear direction first; others are ready for a full rebrand and launch. Each stage needs different priorities.

items.question: How well will you understand my business?
items.teaser: An agency that skips this stage is designing on guesswork.
items.answer: Every project starts with EGGSPLORE, our Brand Audit. Inside the company, we interview your leadership and team to understand the business, its goals and its constraints. Outside, we study your competitors and target market, with a research partner or our in-house team depending on the project. Design only begins once we can explain your business back to you.

items.question: Who will actually work on my project?
items.teaser: Senior people often win the pitch, then hand the work to someone else.
items.answer: Strategy and design sit under one roof, led by a team with 17+ years in branding. You know from the first meeting who leads your project, and the same team stays with you from audit to launch. When specialist partners join for research or activation, we name them up front.

items.question: What exactly am I paying for?
items.teaser: A long list of deliverables means little if you can’t see what each one is for.
items.answer: Every proposal breaks the fee down by item, process, actions, deliverables and quantity, so you can see what each part buys. Depending on the phases you choose, that means audit findings, a brand platform and direction, an identity system, and guidelines your team can use to roll the brand out. What you receive and own at handover is written into the agreement before work starts.

items.question: Is your strategy backed by insights or opinions?
items.teaser: “We like it” is not a reason. Every creative choice should have one.
items.answer: Insights first, then judgment. As a data-driven branding agency, every recommendation we make can be traced back to an audit finding, a business objective or the brand direction you approved. Creative craft still matters, but it works within that rationale, not in place of it.

items.question: How will we know if the branding works?
items.teaser: Branding takes time to pay off, which makes it easy never to measure it at all.
items.answer: We agree on it before the project starts. Brand growth depends on many factors, including product, pricing, distribution and service, so we don’t promise sales figures. Instead we set brand health indicators such as awareness, perception and consistency, measure them at the start, and track them through regular Brand Health Checks so the direction can keep adjusting.

items.question: Have you solved challenges like mine before?
items.teaser: A matching industry in the portfolio is not the same as a matching problem.
items.answer: We look at the challenge before the category: a business that has outgrown its identity, a brand entering a new market, a group of brands that needs a clear structure. Our work spans F&B, FMCG, beauty, property, and corporate and financial services. See examples in Work in your industry below, and ask us for the case closest to yours.

items.question: What happens after the brand launches?
items.teaser: Most brands drift in the months after launch, not before.
items.answer: Through EGGUIDE Guardianship, we can stay on as your brand’s guardian: training your team, reviewing new materials before they go out, and running Brand Health Checks to see how the market perceives you. It’s an optional add-on, so you decide how much support you need.

items.question: Will there be any unexpected costs?
items.teaser: Fees that are vague at the start tend to grow halfway through.
items.answer: Not if we do our job at the proposal stage. Fees are split by phase and item, and the proposal states what is included and what counts as additional work. Third-party costs such as ad spend, talent fees and VAT are listed separately. If the scope changes midway, we quote the change in writing before any work on it begins.
